panel_removed_hint: The worktree was removed. New runs use the project root.

palette_new_thread_placeholder: Pick a project for the new thread

settings_models_hint: New threads start with the default model of their agent.

attachment_add_hint: Attach files. You can also paste images or drop files here.
error_persistence: Could not read or write the local database. Try again, and restart KKCode if it keeps failing.
error_project_path_taken: Another project already uses this folder.
error_project_root_invalid: That path is not a folder. Pick an existing folder.

error_schema: KKCode got data in an unexpected shape. Restart the app, and report a bug if it happens again.
error_ports: Could not inspect or stop the process: {detail}
error_thread_busy: This thread is still running or waiting for approval. Stop it before you archive it.
error_fs_access: Could not read this folder. It may have been moved or deleted.
pr_links_empty: None linked yet. Create one from this branch, or ask an agent to open one.
viewer_binary: This is a binary file, so it is not shown.
viewer_truncated: Showing the first 1 MB of this file.
viewer_changed_on_disk: The file changed on disk after you started editing.
agents_empty: Sub-agents this thread spawns appear here.
agents_missing: Nothing is recorded for this sub-agent.
sidebar_drag_instructions: To reorder, press Space on the handle, move with the arrow keys, then press Space again to drop. Escape cancels.
sidebar_drag_cancel: Reorder cancelled. {title} is back where it was.
sidebar_reorder_failed: Could not save the new order: {message}

home_description: Run Claude Code, Codex and Muse Code on your local repositories. Each thread can get its own git worktree, prepared by your setup script.
settings_slack_hint: Slack mention automations use this token. Slack only allows message search with an xoxp- user token, so give a Slack app the search:read user scope and paste its user OAuth token.
automations_description: Start a thread when a webhook arrives or a new issue or mention shows up. Polling triggers check every minute.
automations_empty_hint: Create one to start threads from webhooks, GitHub or Linear issues, or Slack mentions.
automations_empty_no_project: Add a project first. Every automation starts its threads in a project.
automations_delete_description: Deletes its run history and webhook secret too. Threads it started stay.
automations_bind_loopback_hint: Only programs on this machine can send webhooks.
automations_bind_all_hint: Other devices on your network or tailnet can send webhooks. Each request still needs a valid signature.
automations_dialog_description: Each event renders the prompt template and starts a new thread with it.
automations_trigger_fixed: The trigger type cannot change after creation.
automations_webhook_hint: You get the webhook URL and its signing secret after you create the automation.
automations_repo_hint: owner/name, read with the gh CLI
automations_labels_hint: Optional, comma separated. Issues need every label.
automations_linear_hint: Uses the Linear API key from Integrations. Only issues created after you enable the automation start threads.
automations_slack_hint: Messages that mention this user start threads. Uses the Slack user token from Integrations.
automations_prompt_placeholder: Triage this and propose a fix: {example}
automations_prompt_hint: Placeholders are filled from the event. Missing fields become empty.
automations_worktree_hint: Each run gets its own branch and worktree.
automations_branch_hint: Rendered like the prompt, then made branch-safe. Leave empty to name it after the automation.
automations_enabled_hint: Disabled automations ignore webhooks and stop polling.
automations_webhook_url_hint: POST JSON here, signed with HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body in X-KKCODE-Signature or X-Hub-Signature-256 as sha256=<hex>.
automations_webhook_url_lan_hint: Listening on all interfaces. From another device, use an address it can reach, such as this machine's Tailscale name. Sign the raw body with HMAC-SHA256 in X-KKCODE-Signature or X-Hub-Signature-256.
automations_payload_hint: JSON the prompt template reads, as an event would deliver it. Run now skips duplicate detection.
automations_payload_invalid: The payload is not valid JSON.
automations_secret_description: Configure the sender with this URL and secret. The secret is shown only now.
automations_secret_hint: Store it in the sender now. To get a new one, create a new automation.
project_edit_description: Change the name, folder and setup script of {project}.

settings_account_signed_out_muse: Not signed in. Run muse login in a terminal.

remote_description: Steer threads from the kkcode phone app. The phone connects straight to this machine, so it needs to be on the same network or tailnet.
remote_enable_hint: Paired phones can read threads, answer approvals, send prompts and open terminals in worktrees.
remote_bind_loopback_hint: Only programs on this machine can connect. Choose all interfaces to reach it from a phone.
remote_bind_all_hint: Devices on your network or tailnet can connect. Each one still needs the access token.
remote_network_note: Over Tailscale the connection is encrypted by WireGuard. On a plain LAN it is unencrypted, so keep remote control off on networks you do not trust.

remote_pair_token_hint: The QR code and URL contain the access token. Anyone who scans it can control kkcode.
remote_rotate_hint: Issues a new token and disconnects every paired phone.

site_home_title: kkcode · Agent harness with taste and focus
site_home_description: Run Claude Code and Codex side by side, each in its own worktree. kkcode stays quiet until an agent needs you.
site_pricing_description: kkcode is free. Every feature, with no seats, tiers or trial.
site_backed_tooltip: Not a fund. One person with strong opinions.
site_home_lede: Run Claude Code and Codex side by side, each in its own worktree. kkcode stays quiet while your agents work, and tells you exactly which one needs you.
site_platforms: macOS on Apple Silicon and Linux. Uses the {claude} and {codex} you already signed in to.
site_demo_prompt: Tighten address validation. Canadian postal codes slip through, and a missing country passes.
site_demo_response: I'll make the country check explicit, add a Canadian postal path, and cover both with tests.
site_demo_command_request: Claude Code wants to run a command
site_steer_placeholder: Steer the running turn. Try typing something.
site_demo_hint_idle: The agent waits for you. Nothing else will.
site_demo_hint_working: The agent is working. You could be doing something else.
site_demo_hint_touch: Now it needs you. Tap Allow or Deny.
site_demo_allowed_response: Opened #128 and the checks pass. It's ready for your review.
site_demo_denied_response: Understood. The branch stays local, and the tests are green whenever you want to push.
site_demo_hint_done: Done. That is the whole loop.
site_demo_steered_response: Noted. I'll fold that into the next step without starting over.
site_quiet_description: Most of the time, nothing needs you. The screen should look like it. kkcode spends color on one thing: the thread that is waiting for a human. Glance at the sidebar between other work and you know where to go.
site_legend_working: The agent is busy. Nothing for you to do.
site_legend_needs: An approval, a question, or a setup script that stopped.
site_legend_failed: The turn or the setup failed. The log is one click away.
site_legend_done: Finished, with the pull request and its merge state linked.
site_features_heading: Everything around the loop. Nothing in its way.
site_features_description: Start a thread, steer it, review what changed, ship the PR. kkcode handles the parts between, so the agent output stays the content.
site_feature_worktree_description: Every thread gets its own branch and checkout. Your setup script copies the {env} in one line.
site_feature_approvals_description: Commands, edits and MCP calls wait inside the conversation. Allow once, or for the session.
site_feature_steer_description: Send another message while the agent works. No stop, no restart, no lost context.
site_feature_mcp_description: Both agents can review their diff, link a pull request and read Linear. Every call is scoped to one thread.
site_feature_pr_description: Draft, open, merged or closed, with CI checks and the review decision. Refreshed every minute.
site_feature_ports_description: The dev servers a thread started, listed by port. Stop one without hunting for a PID.
site_feature_automations_description: Start a thread from a signed webhook, a new GitHub issue, a Linear ticket or a Slack mention.
site_feature_setup_description: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and skills load from the project and your home, the same as in the CLIs.
site_keyboard_description: Every frequent action has a shortcut. Every shortcut can be rebound, with chord recording and conflict detection built in.
site_keyboard_note: Go on, press a few. The keys will press back.
site_simple_description: Every feature here was shipped by agents running inside kkcode. When the loop hurts while we work, that is a product bug, and it gets fixed.
site_number_channel: channel between the UI and the app
site_faq_what_answer: A desktop app that runs Claude Code and Codex side by side. Each thread can live in its own git worktree, and the sidebar shows which one needs you.
site_faq_agents_answer: Claude Code through the Agent SDK, and Codex through its app-server protocol. Pick the agent and the model for each thread.
site_faq_keys_question: Do I need new API keys?
site_faq_keys_answer: No. kkcode uses the {claude} and {codex} CLIs you are already signed in to.
site_faq_code_answer: Nowhere new. Agents run on your machine against your repositories. Keys such as a Linear token are kept in the OS keychain.
site_faq_editor_answer: No. kkcode is the harness around the agent loop: start, steer, review, ship. Open the worktree in your editor whenever you want to.
site_faq_price_answer: Nothing. Every feature is free, with no seats, tiers or trial. {pricing}.
site_faq_platforms_answer: macOS on Apple Silicon, and Linux as an AppImage.
site_closing_description: One window. Every agent. Only the ones that need you ask for you.
site_footer_credit: Backed by Kalan. Built with kkcode.
site_pricing_lede: No seats, no tiers, no trial that runs out. Every feature on this site is in the one plan, and the one plan costs nothing.
site_plan_note: No account. No card. Nothing to cancel.
site_receipt_label: A receipt for kkcode that totals zero dollars
site_costs_description: kkcode runs the {claude} and {codex} CLIs you are already signed in to. Your usage goes to those plans, the same as it does in a terminal.
site_costs_kkcode: $0. The harness, the worktrees, the MCP server and every update.
site_costs_plans: Whatever plan or API key you already use. kkcode adds no markup and never sits between you and them.
